title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
authors: Kai Greshake, Sahar Abdelnabi, Shailesh Mishra, Christoph Endres, Thorsten Holz, Mario Fritz
relevance: Introduces indirect prompt injection via retrieved data; foundational threat model for TrustBound.

title: Ignore Previous Prompt: Attack Techniques For Language Models
authors: Fábio Perez, Ian Ribeiro
relevance: Early goal-hijacking / prompt-leaking attacks (PromptInject); direct-injection baseline.

title: Formalizing and Benchmarking Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses
authors: Yupei Liu, Yuqi Jia, Runpeng Geng, Jinyuan Jia, Neil Zhenqiang Gong
relevance: Formal framework + benchmark of 5 attacks / 10 defenses; evaluates paraphrasing as a prevention defense (partial ASR reduction, substantial utility cost).

title: Baseline Defenses for Adversarial Attacks Against Aligned Language Models
authors: Neel Jain et al.
relevance: Baseline defenses incl. paraphrasing for optimizer-based jailbreaks; origin of paraphrase-as-defense idea and its utility cost.

title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
authors: Edoardo Debenedetti, Jie Zhang, Mislav Balunović, Luca Beurer-Kellner, Marc Fischer, Florian Tramèr
relevance: Standard dynamic agent IPI benchmark (97 tasks, 629 security cases); expected baseline environment.

title: InjecAgent: Benchmarking Indirect Prompt Injections in Tool-Integrated Large Language Model Agents
authors: Qiusi Zhan, Zhixiang Liang, Zifan Ying, Daniel Kang
relevance: Tool-integrated agent IPI benchmark (1,054 cases); direct-harm vs exfiltration attack taxonomy.

title: Agent Security Bench (ASB): Formalizing and Benchmarking Attacks and Defenses in LLM-based Agents
authors: Hanrong Zhang et al.
relevance: Agent Security Bench: broad attack/defense benchmark across 10 scenarios and 13 backbones.

title: Benchmarking and Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on Large Language Models
authors: Jingwei Yi et al.
relevance: BIPIA benchmark; proposes boundary-awareness and explicit-reminder defenses, the closest prior form of TrustBound's boundary-reminder baseline.

title: WASP: Benchmarking Web Agent Security Against Prompt Injection Attacks
authors: Ivan Evtimov, Arman Zharmagambetov, Aaron Grattafiori, Chuan Guo, Kamalika Chaudhuri
relevance: Web-agent IPI benchmark; 'security by incompetence' finding (partial vs full attacker-goal completion).

title: AgentDyn: Are Your Agent Security Defenses Deployable in Real-World Dynamic Environments?
authors: Hao Li, Ruoyao Wen, Shanghao Shi, Ning Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik, Chaowei Xiao
relevance: Dynamic open-ended agent IPI benchmark with helpful third-party instructions; most defenses insecure or over-defend.

title: Security Challenges in AI Agent Deployment: Insights from a Large Scale Public Competition
authors: Andy Zou et al.
relevance: Large public agent red-teaming competition (1.8M attacks) and ART benchmark; robustness weakly correlated with capability.

title: LLMail-Inject: A Dataset from a Realistic Adaptive Prompt Injection Challenge
authors: Sahar Abdelnabi et al.
relevance: 208k human-written adaptive attacks requiring retrieval + correct unauthorized tool-call arguments; email-agent setting similar to TrustBound.

title: AutoDojo: A Generative Benchmark for Evaluating Prompt Injection Defenses in LLM Agents
authors: Xinhang Ma, Taoran Li, Chaowei Xiao, Zhiyuan Yu, Ning Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik
relevance: Adaptive black-box IPI generation on AgentDojo/AgentDyn; static benchmarks overestimate defenses; under-specified tasks most vulnerable.

title: INFUSE: A Unified Surface Benchmark for Indirect Prompt Injection in Agentic Systems
authors: Thuy Dung Nguyen, Jingyi Guo, Rana Seda Dubauskas, Sreepriya Damuluru, Taylor T. Johnson, Kevin Leach
relevance: Long-horizon IPI benchmark; finds LLM paraphrasing of observations an unreliable defense (can increase ASR for some models).

title: The Instruction Hierarchy: Training LLMs to Prioritize Privileged Instructions
authors: Eric Wallace, Kai Xiao, Reimar Leike, Lilian Weng, Johannes Heidecke, Alex Beutel
relevance: OpenAI instruction hierarchy (system > user > tool outputs); the trained prior that TrustBound's channel manipulation probes.

title: StruQ: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Structured Queries
authors: Sizhe Chen, Julien Piet, Chawin Sitawarin, David Wagner
relevance: Structured queries: separate prompt/data channels + fine-tuning; channel-separation defense.

title: SecAlign: Defending Against Prompt Injection with Preference Optimization
authors: Sizhe Chen, Arman Zharmagambetov, Saeed Mahloujifar, Kamalika Chaudhuri, David Wagner, Chuan Guo
relevance: Preference-optimization defense against prompt injection; model-level baseline.

title: Meta-SecAlign: Training LLMs against Prompt Injection for Robust Agents
authors: Sizhe Chen, Arman Zharmagambetov, David Wagner, Chuan Guo
relevance: Follow-up to SecAlign: reports SecAlign utility degradation in agentic tasks at scale; Meta-SecAlign open models trained against injection.

title: Defending Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks With Spotlighting
authors: Keegan Hines, Gary Lopez, Matthew Hall, Federico Zarfati, Yonatan Zunger, Emre Kiciman
relevance: Input transformations that give a continuous provenance signal; closest prompting analogue of TrustBound's provenance-preserving label condition.

title: Can LLMs Separate Instructions From Data? And What Do We Even Mean By That?
authors: Egor Zverev, Sahar Abdelnabi, Soroush Tabesh, Mario Fritz, Christoph H. Lampert
relevance: Formal measure + SEP dataset for instruction/data separation; all models fail to achieve high separation.

title: Control Illusion: The Failure of Instruction Hierarchies in Large Language Models
authors: Yilin Geng et al.
relevance: System/user separation fails to establish reliable hierarchy; social-authority framings matter more than roles.

title: Prompt Injection as Role Confusion
authors: Charles Ye, Jasmine Cui, Dylan Hadfield-Menell
relevance: Models infer role from how text sounds, not its tag; mechanism for why channel/label presentation matters.

title: Same Payload, Different Channel: Measuring Trust Asymmetry in Tool-Using Language Models
authors: Mohammed Sameer Syed, Rozhin Yasaei
relevance: Matched payloads varied only by channel (user vs tool metadata vs tool output); tool outputs treated as data, user channel more authoritative.

title: Position, Role or Label? A Controlled Study of Instruction Conflicts in LLM Agents
authors: Anish Laddha, Nitesh Pradhan, Gaurav Srivastava
relevance: Controlled study separating position, chat role and text label in instruction conflicts; directly relevant to TrustBound's channel-vs-label ablation.

title: Where You Inject Matters: The Trust Region Effect in LLM Agents
authors: Chengquan Guo et al.
relevance: Fixed payload, varied placement: agents assign different implicit trust to environment regions.

title: Auditing Provenance Sensitivity in LLM Agent Action Selection
authors: Junchi Liao et al.
relevance: Holds proposition fixed and varies only its source authority; models respond to textual source cues but untrusted evidence still influences actions.

title: When Context Gets Root: Privilege Escalation in LLM Harnesses
authors: Xingbang He et al.
relevance: Instruction privilege escalation: harness delegation re-inserts tool-level content as user/system messages; the real-world version of TrustBound's provenance-lost condition.

title: What's in Your Agent's Context? Context Privilege Escalation Attacks against AI Agent Harness
authors: Zichuan Li, Jian Cui, Ashley Chen, Xiaojing Liao, Luyi Xing
relevance: Context privilege escalation in 12 real agent harnesses: low-privilege content incorporated into higher-privilege message roles.

title: Defeating Prompt Injections by Design
authors: Edoardo Debenedetti et al.
relevance: CaMeL: control/data flow from trusted query + capabilities enforced at tool calls; template for TrustBound's structured authorization check.

title: The Dual LLM pattern for building AI assistants that can resist prompt injection
authors: Simon Willison
relevance: Dual LLM pattern: privileged vs quarantined LLM with variable references; warns quarantined output must never reach the privileged LLM unfiltered.

title: Securing AI Agents with Information-Flow Control
authors: Manuel Costa et al.
relevance: FIDES: IFC planner tracking confidentiality/integrity labels with deterministic policy enforcement; closest design to TrustBound's taint tracker.

title: RTBAS: Defending LLM Agents Against Prompt Injection and Privacy Leakage
authors: Peter Yong Zhong et al.
relevance: IFC for tool-based agents with LM-judge and attention-saliency dependency screeners; selective label propagation.

title: System-Level Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks: An Information Flow Control Perspective
authors: Fangzhou Wu, Ethan Cecchetti, Chaowei Xiao
relevance: f-secure LLM system: IFC-based disaggregated planner with security monitor filtering untrusted input into planning.

title: IsolateGPT: An Execution Isolation Architecture for LLM-Based Agentic Systems
authors: Yuhao Wu, Franziska Roesner, Tadayoshi Kohno, Ning Zhang, Umar Iqbal
relevance: Execution isolation architecture for LLM app ecosystems.

title: Progent: Securing AI Agents with Privilege Control
authors: Tianneng Shi et al.
relevance: Programmable privilege control: LLM-generated symbolic tool-call policy from user task, deterministic enforcement.

title: Design Patterns for Securing LLM Agents against Prompt Injections
authors: Luca Beurer-Kellner et al.
relevance: Six design patterns (action-selector, plan-then-execute, map-reduce, dual LLM, code-then-execute, context-minimization) with provable resistance.

title: MELON: Provable Defense Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks in AI Agents
authors: Kaijie Zhu, Xianjun Yang, Jindong Wang, Wenbo Guo, William Yang Wang
relevance: Masked re-execution detects actions that do not depend on the user task.

title: The Task Shield: Enforcing Task Alignment to Defend Against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM Agents
authors: Feiran Jia, Tong Wu, Xin Qin, Anna Squicciarini
relevance: Test-time task-alignment verification of every instruction/tool call.

title: DRIFT: Dynamic Rule-Based Defense with Injection Isolation for Securing LLM Agents
authors: Hao Li, Xiaogeng Liu, Hung-Chun Chiu, Dianqi Li, Ning Zhang, Chaowei Xiao
relevance: Secure planner + dynamic validator + injection isolator that masks conflicting instructions in memory.

title: PromptArmor: Simple yet Effective Prompt Injection Defenses
authors: Tianneng Shi et al.
relevance: Off-the-shelf LLM detects and removes injected prompts before the agent; recommended as standard baseline.

title: DataSentinel: A Game-Theoretic Detection of Prompt Injection Attacks
authors: Yupei Liu, Yuqi Jia, Jinyuan Jia, Dawn Song, Neil Zhenqiang Gong
relevance: Game-theoretic fine-tuned injection detector robust to adaptive attacks.

title: LlamaFirewall: An open source guardrail system for building secure AI agents
authors: Sahana Chennabasappa et al.
relevance: Meta guardrail system: PromptGuard 2, AlignmentCheck (CoT auditor), CodeShield; LLM-monitor baseline.

title: Get my drift? Catching LLM Task Drift with Activation Deltas
authors: Sahar Abdelnabi, Aideen Fay, Giovanni Cherubin, Ahmed Salem, Mario Fritz, Andrew Paverd
relevance: Activation-delta probes detect task drift caused by external data.

title: Permissive Information-Flow Analysis for Large Language Models
authors: Shoaib Ahmed Siddiqui et al.
relevance: Label propagation through LLM queries: propagate only labels of influential inputs vs conservative 'output inherits all input labels'.

title: Can Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks Be Detected and Removed?
authors: Yulin Chen et al.
relevance: Benchmarks detection and removal (segmentation/extraction) of indirect injections; removal as sanitization.

title: Firewalls to Secure Dynamic LLM Agentic Networks
authors: Sahar Abdelnabi, Amr Gomaa, Eugene Bagdasarian, Per Ola Kristensson, Reza Shokri
relevance: Language-converter firewall projects inter-agent messages onto a closed structured protocol, structurally eliminating embedded instructions.

title: The Granularity Mismatch in Agent Security: Argument-Level Provenance Solves Enforcement and Isolates the LLM Reasoning Bottleneck
authors: Linfeng Fan, Ziwei Li, Yuan Tian, Yichen Wang, Rongsheng Li, Xiong Wang
relevance: Argument-level provenance contracts; under oracle provenance perfect enforcement, bottleneck shifts to provenance inference.

title: ROPE: Routed Origin Policy Enforcement against Indirect Prompt Injection
authors: Xinhang Ma, Chaowei Xiao, William Yeoh, Ning Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik
relevance: Deterministic origin check: values reaching state-changing tools must trace to user or user-named sources; rewording-invariant.

title: Ghost in the Agent: Redefining Information Flow Tracking for LLM Agents
authors: Yuandao Cai, Wensheng Tang, Cheng Wen, Shengchao Qin
relevance: Offline taint tracking for agents covering semantic transformation (incl. summarization) and causal influence; compares to FIDES.

title: Agent Privilege Separation in OpenClaw: A Structural Defense Against Prompt Injection
authors: Darren Cheng, Wen-Kwang Tsao
relevance: Reader/actor privilege-separated pipeline with JSON summaries; summaries can still carry actionable injected content.

title: Lessons from Defending Gemini Against Indirect Prompt Injections
authors: Chongyang Shi et al.
relevance: Google DeepMind adaptive IPI evaluation of Gemini; includes paraphrasing baseline and argues adaptive evaluation is necessary.

title: Prompt Infection: LLM-to-LLM Prompt Injection within Multi-Agent Systems
authors: Donghyun Lee, Mo Tiwari
relevance: Self-replicating LLM-to-LLM injection through multi-agent pipelines that include summarizer agents; LLM Tagging (source tagging) alone reduces ASR only ~5%.

title: Multi-Agent Systems Execute Arbitrary Malicious Code
authors: Harold Triedman, Rishi Jha, Vitaly Shmatikov
relevance: MAS hijacking: adversarial content laundered through sub-agent outputs/metadata reaches orchestrators; succeeds even when agents resist direct/indirect PI.

title: Trust Cascade through Provenance Erasure: How Multi-Agent Delegation Breaks Single-Agent Safety
authors: Yuxin Zhou et al.
relevance: Closest prior work: delegation strips provenance markers but keeps payload; delegation-as-user replay attributes amplification to channel escalation, not content reformulation.

title: Kill-Chain Canaries: Stage-Level Tracking of Prompt Injection Across Attack Surfaces and Five Production LLMs
authors: Haochuan Kevin Wang, Zechen Zhang
relevance: Canary tokens tracked Exposed->Persisted->Relayed->Executed; measures whether writer/summarizer stages strip or relay injections.

title: Can CaMeLs Talk? Securing Multi-Agent Systems Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
authors: James Peters-Gill, Avi Semler, Henning Bartsch, Ilia Shumailov, Christian Schroeder de Witt
relevance: CaMeL guarantees do not compose across agents ('boundary laundering'); multi-CaMeL preserves provenance via separate data channel; MultiAgentDojo.

title: OMNI-LEAK: Orchestrator Multi-Agent Network Induced Data Leakage
authors: Akshat Naik et al.
relevance: Single IPI compromises SQL agent, orchestrator and notification agent despite access control.

title: Autonomous LLM Agent Worms: Cross-Platform Propagation, Automated Discovery and Temporal Re-Entry Defense
authors: Mingming Zha, Xiaofeng Wang
relevance: Persistent agent worms with payloads optimized to survive LLM summarization/paraphrasing across hops; typed memory promotion defense.

title: Safe to Check, Unsafe to Use: Relinking at the Compression Boundary of LLM Agents
authors: Zesen Liu, Zihan Zhang, Dongdong She
relevance: Summarization-based compression can synthesize a complete malicious instruction from benign fragments ('relinking').

title: Governance Decay: How Context Compaction Silently Erases Safety Constraints in Long-Horizon LLM Agents
authors: Shiyang Chen
relevance: Context compaction drops safety constraints; adversarial content can bias the summarizer to omit a policy.

title: When Do Summaries Become Instructions? Unsupported Policy in LLM Agents' Self-Written Handoff Summaries
authors: Wenhui Chu
relevance: Self-written handoff summaries sometimes state unsupported authorizations that change successor actions.

title: Trust propagation and structural containment in Multi-agent LLM pipelines
authors: Tanzim Hossain Safin, Sharif Noor Zisad, Swakkhar Shatabda, Ragib Hasan
relevance: Four-agent pipeline: validator judgment compromised but independent authorization layer contains execution; supports structural authorization.

title: Adaptive Attacks Break Defenses Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM Agents
authors: Qiusi Zhan, Richard Fang, Henil Shalin Panchal, Daniel Kang
relevance: Adaptive attacks bypass 8 IPI defenses with >50% ASR.

title: The Attacker Moves Second: Stronger Adaptive Attacks Bypass Defenses Against Llm Jailbreaks and Prompt Injections
authors: Milad Nasr et al.
relevance: Adaptive attacks (gradient, RL, search, human) bypass 12 defenses, most >90% ASR; fixed-payload evaluations are insufficient.

title: Adaptive Attacks on Trusted Monitors Subvert AI Control Protocols
authors: Mikhail Terekhov et al.
relevance: Prompt injections in agent outputs subvert LLM monitors in AI control protocols.

title: SHADE-Arena: Evaluating Sabotage and Monitoring in LLM Agents
authors: Jonathan Kutasov et al.
relevance: Sabotage + monitoring benchmark; best monitor AUC 0.87; hidden scratchpad matters.

title: AI Control: Improving Safety Despite Intentional Subversion
authors: Ryan Greenblatt, Buck Shlegeris, Kshitij Sachan, Fabien Roger
relevance: Defines AI control protocols (trusted monitoring/editing, untrusted monitoring).

title: Ctrl-Z: Controlling AI Agents via Resampling
authors: Aryan Bhatt et al.
relevance: First agentic control evaluation (BashBench); resample protocols.

title: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
authors: Neil Kale et al.
relevance: Monitor red teaming: agent awareness dominates monitor awareness; extra monitor information less helpful than expected.

title: How does information access affect LLM monitors' ability to detect sabotage?
authors: Rauno Arike, Raja Mehta Moreno, Rohan Subramani, Shubhorup Biswas, Francis Rhys Ward
relevance: Less-is-more effect: LLM monitors often perform better with less information; extract-and-evaluate monitoring.

title: Blocking at the Boundary: Auditing Long-Horizon Agents against Staged Prompt Injection
authors: Jingkai Liu, Yufei Han, Xiaoting Lyu, Wei Wang, Ting Yu
relevance: Boundary action auditing for staged injection in Claude Code/Codex; attribution-based auditor traces attacker-reachable sources of action elements.

title: Mitigating prompt injections in browser use
authors: Anthropic (no individual authors listed)
relevance: RL training + classifiers + red teaming for browser-agent IPI; residual adaptive Best-of-N ASR 1.4-2.4% with improved safeguards; states the problem is far from solved.

title: How we built Claude Code auto mode: a safer way to skip permissions
authors: John Hughes
relevance: Production action classifier deliberately sees only user messages + tool calls (no tool outputs, no assistant prose); notes the cost that it cannot always tell where an identifier came from. Direct motivation for monitor-provenance question.

title: Recommendations for Technical AI Safety Research Directions
authors: Anthropic Alignment Science team (no individual authors listed)
relevance: Lists AI control / behavioral monitoring (monitor failures concentrated where actor is malicious; actors with message passing) and hijacking agents via website content as directions.

title: SHADE-Arena: Evaluating sabotage and monitoring in LLM agents
authors: Anthropic (blog post accompanying Kutasov et al.)
relevance: Blog summary of SHADE-Arena: 17 task pairs, monitor not told the side task, 80/100 suspicion threshold; monitoring subtle sabotage is hard.
